output.brief:
The five rejected containers were all booked through the new documentation suite for Meridane, and each was set to carry mandarins at 7.0°C. That setting was copied from the avocado product record on 1 Aug and never changed. Your own specification is 4.0°C. The carrier's units held 7.0°C within 0.4°C of the setpoint, so Meridane did what it was told. Every container at 4.0°C passed, including the one Meridane container on the old email booking. The new fungicide is not the cause: one rejected container used old stock, and four Pellacor containers at 4°C passed. Transit time does not explain it either. Lower Serra fruit shows more decay inside the rejected containers, but it was 28–40% of every container, including the ones that passed. That is a minor factor at most, not a reason to suspend growers.

Next steps, in order. First, correct the mandarin record to 4.0°C. Second, have Meridane reset the container at sea and the one queued for 10 Oct. Third, add a check of reefer settings against product specifications before each submission. Do not lodge the Meridane claim, suspend Lower Serra or revert the fungicide. Hold off on penalising Brindle, because your own sign-off also missed the error. I am quite confident in this diagnosis.
